sections.title: Climate
sections.filled: Across the surrounding basin of about 4,662 km², rainfall averages about 134 mm a year, clearly seasonal, with August the wettest month. Temperatures there average -11.3 °C, from -26.8 °C in February to 6.1 °C in July. Of the four basins that meet here, it receives the least precipitation. Compared with the three basins around it, its basin is cooler than two and is more arid than two.

sections.title: Land and geology
sections.filled: Across the basin, the land is very gently sloping on average (a mean slope of 1.4%), with topsoil that averages 48% sand, 36% silt and 16% clay (USDA texture class: loam). The underlying rock is mostly siliciclastic sedimentary rocks. Permafrost underlies about 97% of it.

sections.title: Surroundings
sections.filled: Utqiagvik's basin is one of four that meet here. None of them drains into it. It drains into none of them. The basins across its divides are all higher. Of the four basins that meet here, it has the lowest mean elevation, the least relief and the gentlest slopes.

sections.title: About these figures
sections.filled: The elevation and ecoregion under Setting are for Utqiagvik itself. The other figures describe the basin of about 4,662 km² that contains it, from global datasets. 3 measures are zero here and so have no percentile: Cropland extent, Karst area, Pasture extent. Elevation and distances are measured from the place's point in WHG, which may be the centre of a town rather than its shore or riverbank.
